newsitem.title: INDIA: India issues travel permits to 37,500 Gulf workers.
newsitem.headline: India issues travel permits to 37,500 Gulf workers.

text.p: India said on Tuesday it had issued emergency travel documents to about 37,500 expatriate workers in the United Arab Emirates who are escaping a tough new labour law targeting illegal workers.
Indian diplomatic offices in Dubai and Abu Dhabi have been flooded with applications for exit permits from illegal workers rushing to leave before an amnesty expires on September 30.

"We have no idea of the number of people (Indians) leaving," K.C. Singh, a senior foreign ministry official coordinating the return of the workers, told reporters. "We have asked the Dubai and Abu Dhabi officials, but there is chaos at their end, too."
The emergency certificates allow Indians without proper travel documents to make a one-way trip back to India.

Singh said most Indians working in the UAE -- about 500,000 -- had valid travel documents and no crisis influx of workers was expected. He estimated only about 10 percent of Indian workers in the UAE were there illegally.
The two main national airlines, Air-India and Indian Airlines, have put on special flights in addition to their weekly schedule of 32 flights to the UAE, Singh said.
The majority of the returning workers have had menial jobs as housemaid workers or labourers, and often earned too little to afford their own air fares.
